name: show_plan
description: Show the player "Here's the plan" on one screen: a one-line summary, how to play, and the four rules that matter most, with every rule in spec.md one stick-press away. Call it after the questions, once spec.md is written and before any game code. The player either says build, or asks to change something. After a change, update spec.md (the rules and the Changelog) and call show_plan again with the new rules. Also call it again, with `changes`, if what a rule means has to change during the build. A check bug that leaves the rule's meaning alone doesn't come here. Rule text must be plain words a 10-year-old understands, never code. The result is JSON text: {"choice":"build"} or {"choice":"change","said":"<what the player wants changed>"}.

summary.description: One sentence: what the game is.

controls.description: How to play, from the spec's Controls: what the stick and buttons do, in kid words, at most 80 characters. Example: "Stick: slide. A: jump."

top_rules.description: The ids of the four rules that matter most to the player, in the order to show them. Include every rule the player will check (you-check).

rules.description: Every rule in spec.md, in order.

id.description: Rule id from the spec, e.g. R3.

kind.description: auto: the playtest proves it. you-check: the player checks it on first play.

was.description: Only for a change to an existing game: the rule's words before this change. Leave it out for a rule that stays the same or is new.

new.description: Only for a change: true for a rule this change adds.

changes.description: Only when you call this again after the first playtest: each rule whose meaning changed, and what changed in the spec, in plain words.

text.description: What changed and why, in plain words.
